newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania Sanevit trading remains halted.
newsitem.headline: Romania Sanevit trading remains halted.

text.p: Romanian listed syringe maker Sanevit SA said bourse trading in its shares, halted a month ago, would remain suspended until end-1996 pending an announcement on adding imported equipment to its capital base.

"A shareholders' meeting decided on including imported equipment into our capital, but we need an assessment of that equipment first," company manager Mircea Roman said from the headquarters in the Transylvanian city of Arad on Thursday.
Sanevit, the country's sole producer of disposable syringes, bought equipment from Italy's Penta Group on a $37 million credit guaranteed by the Romanian state. Its share capital is 24.7 billion lei.
Roman said accountants Coopers & Lybrand were assessing the equipment. He did not expect assessment procedures to be completed before the end of the year.
"So, Sanevit will not trade for some time," he said.

Sanevit started production in April 1995 with a targeted annual output of 180 million syringes and 400 million needles. The domestic market can absorb up to 300 million syringes and 400 million needles annually.
In May, the company signed a 10 billion lei contract to supply 62 million disposable syringes and 2.89 million needles to the Health Ministry this year. Roman said the contract was on track.
The company posted a six-month net profit of 518.9 million lei this year, up from 377.8 million in the year-ago period.
Sanevit entered trading when the stock exchange opened a year ago and once dominated trading. But it has fallen sharply in the thin interest plaguing the Romanian capital market.

Before trading in Sanevit shares was halted four weeks ago, the company closed at 9,100 lei, compared with a 71,000 lei price last November. ($=3,687 lei) -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
